source: English Wikipedia island lists and articles, with Wikimedia Commons photographs confirmed on 27 October 2026

rows.title: Joined to Ceallasaigh Beag
rows.evidence: The list says Ceallasaigh Mòr and Ceallasaigh Beag, in Loch Maddy, North Uist, are each about 50 hectares at high tide, and that at low tide they are connected to one another and to several smaller tidal islets.
rows.reject_reason: The photograph is of Ceallasaigh Beag from the air. Ceallasaigh Mòr is only a clouded edge of that frame, so the picture is not of Keallasay More or of the tidal link.
rows.summary: Keallasay More is Ceallasaigh Mòr, in Loch Maddy off North Uist. At high tide it is a separate island of about 50 hectares. At low tide it is connected to Ceallasaigh Beag and to several smaller tidal islets in the shallow lagoon around them. The link is exposed at low tide and covered at high tide.

rows.title: Joined to the other Crowlin Islands
rows.evidence: The list says the Crowlin Islands, in the Inner Sound off Raasay, are three separate islands at high tide and a single island at low tide. The Commons description of the linking beach says it forms the head of Crowlin Harbour at low tide and is submerged at high tide.
rows.summary: Eilean Mòr is the largest of the Crowlin Islands, in the Inner Sound off Raasay. The three Crowlin Islands are separate at high tide and form one island at low tide. The beach between Eilean Mòr and Eilean Meadhonach is exposed at low tide and submerged at high tide.

rows.title: Smallest of the Crowlin Islands
rows.evidence: The list says the Crowlin Islands are three separate islands at high tide and a single island at low tide. The Commons description of the shore photograph names this rock as the smallest Crowlin isle.
rows.summary: Eilean Beag is the smallest of the Crowlin Islands, in the Inner Sound off Raasay. The three Crowlin Islands are separate at high tide and form one island at low tide. The links between them are exposed at low tide and covered at high tide.
rows.commons_file: File:Shore, North of Eilean Beag - geograph.org.uk - 499914.jpg

rows.title: Connected to St Mary's
rows.evidence: The St Mary's article says the island's area includes four small tidal islands which connect with St Mary's at low tide: Toll's Island, Taylor's Island, Newford Island, and the island at Innisidgen.
rows.summary: Taylor's Island is one of four small tidal islands that connect with St Mary's in the Isles of Scilly at low tide, with Toll's Island, Newford Island, and the island at Innisidgen. The link to St Mary's is exposed at low tide and covered at high tide.

rows.title: Tidal islet in Porthloo
rows.evidence: The St Mary's article names Newford Island as one of four small tidal islands which connect with St Mary's at low tide. The Commons description of the Porthloo photograph says that at high tide almost all of the island visible there would be covered.
rows.summary: Newford Island is one of four small tidal islands that connect with St Mary's at low tide, on the southern edge of Porthloo. At high tide almost all of the island seen from that bay is covered. The link to St Mary's is exposed at low tide and covered at high tide.

rows.title: The island at Innisidgen
rows.evidence: The St Mary's article says the island at Innisidgen is one of four small tidal islands which connect with St Mary's at low tide.
rows.reject_reason: The photograph is a sign on St Mary's pointing to the Innisidgen burial chamber, with the mainland shore in the foreground. It is not a photograph of the tidal island or of the link that joins it to St Mary's.
rows.summary: Innisidgen is the island at Innisidgen, one of four small tidal islands that connect with St Mary's at low tide, with Toll's Island, Taylor's Island, and Newford Island. The link to St Mary's is exposed at low tide and covered at high tide.

rows.title: Split by tidal channels
rows.evidence: The article says Burntwick Island lies among the tidal sand banks of the Medway, separated from the Chetney Marshes by Stangate Creek, and that narrow tidal channels cross it so that at high tide the island is separated into several smaller islands.
rows.reject_reason: The Burntwick Island article says Stangate Creek separates the island from Chetney Marshes, and that creeks across the marsh split it into pieces at high tide. It does not say a drying link joins the island to the mainland, or to another island, and is covered at high tide.
rows.summary: Burntwick Island is a flat marsh on the tidal sand banks of the Medway, separated from the Chetney Marshes by Stangate Creek. Narrow tidal channels cross it, and at high tide those channels separate the island into several smaller islands. The ground between those parts is exposed at low tide and covered at high tide.

rows.title: Sand bank from Skerries
rows.evidence: The article says Shenick Island lies east of Skerries, County Dublin, and that it may be reached by boat but at low tide it may be reached by crossing a sand bank.
rows.summary: Shenick Island lies east of Skerries in County Dublin. It may be reached by boat, and at low tide it may be reached by crossing a sand bank from the shore. That sand bank is exposed at low tide and covered at high tide.

rows.title: Rocks to Sgeir nam Feusgan
rows.evidence: The photograph's description says a line of rocks exposed at low tide links Eilean Fada Beag to Sgeir nam Feusgan.
rows.summary: A line of rocks links Eilean Fada Beag to Sgeir nam Feusgan. The rocks are exposed at low tide. The line is uncovered at low tide and covered at high tide, so the two islets are joined only while the tide is out.

rows.title: Tidal path to Danna
rows.source_title: Tidal path from Eilean nan Uan to the Island of Danna
rows.evidence: The photograph's description names a tidal path from Eilean nan Uan to the Island of Danna. This is the Eilean nan Uan beside Danna, not the other islands of that name.
rows.summary: A tidal path runs from Eilean nan Uan to the Island of Danna. The path is the drying link between the two islands. It is exposed at low tide and covered at high tide.
